findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` on the dataclass captures the timestamp when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is constructed. Every instance created without an explicit `queued` value (e.g. via `from_integration`) will carry the same stale process-start time, defeating the field's apparent purpose of recording when the assignment change was queued. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Task now passes `assignment_source` kwarg to provider `sync_assignee_outbound` implementations that were not updated
findings.body: The task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but none of the concrete provider implementations (Jira, VSTS/GitHub, etc. — none are in this PR's changed files) declare an `assignment_source` parameter; the abstract method in `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` also still has signature `(external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)`. For implementations that don't accept `**kwargs`, every outbound assignee sync for an issue-sync-enabled org will now raise `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'`, breaking assignee sync entirely. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` signature (issues.py line ~397) was not updated to include the parameter, unlike `sync_status_outbound`.

findings.title: `from_dict` silently returns None on malformed input, disabling cycle prevention
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns `None` if the dict doesn't match the constructor (e.g. unknown keys from a stale producer, or a `queued` value of the wrong shape). When that happens in `sync_assignee_outbound` (task line 53-55), `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)` returns True and the outbound sync proceeds — i.e. exactly the sync-loop this PR is meant to prevent is silently re-enabled for any malformed payload, with no logging to surface the parse failure. At minimum the failure should be logged.

findings.title: Round-trip through dict does not preserve `queued` as a datetime
findings.body: `to_dict()` serializes `queued` via `asdict` into a `datetime`, and `from_dict()` reconstructs it via `cls(**input_dict)`. Since dataclasses do not validate types, a payload where `queued` arrives as a string (e.g. after JSON serialization through Celery/Redis in some configurations) will be accepted silently, leaving `queued` as a `str`. Any future consumer relying on `queued` being a `datetime` (ordering, comparisons) will fail or behave incorrectly; there is no coercion or rejection in `from_dict`.

findings.title: Inbound assignee sync ignores organization scoping for the assignment source check
findings.body: In `sync_group_assignee_inbound`, `where_should_sync(integration, "inbound_assignee")` is called without an `organization_id`, so groups from all orgs with the integration are affected and assigned an `AssignmentSource` for the integration. That part is fine, but note the companion outbound path in `where_should_sync` (line 48) calls `should_sync(key)` with no sync source; this is the status path so it is currently correct, but if `AssignmentSource` propagation is later extended to status sync, this call site will need updating — worth confirming intent, since the `sync_status_outbound` abstract signature was changed in this PR to accept `assignment_source` yet no caller passes one, leaving dead API surface that is untested.
